content: ABCA3, or ATP-binding cassette sub-family A member 3, is a protein encoded by the ABCA3 gene in humans. This protein is associated with cellular membranes and belongs to the superfamily of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. ABC transporters are responsible for the translocation of various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. The ABC genes are categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. ABCA3 is specifically a member of the ABC1 subfamily. Notably, the ABC1 subfamily is the only major ABC subfamily that is exclusively found in multicellular eukaryotic organisms. The full-length transporter encoded by the ABCA3 gene is thought to play a role in the development of resistance to xenobiotics (foreign chemical substances) and in the process of engulfment during programmed cell death (apoptosis). Clinical Significance Mutations in the ABCA3 gene are associated with cataract-microcornea syndrome. Additionally, these mutations are linked to surfactant metabolism dysfunction type 3, a condition that affects the proper functioning of pulmonary surfactants.
